surfaces.part: curled crossarm with gold end caps

answer.evidence: The main body is the square stone pedestal at rows 35-45 (width 14). Its light top face fills rows 35-39. A front-edge line at about row 40 is followed by a darker band at rows 40-41, then the gray front face down to row 45, so the top and front face are both clear. The two lantern roofs are sloped blue planes above eave lines at rows 18-19 (width 27-28), which counts as evidence (c). The post is a thin shaft, and the star finial is decor. The crossarm is a thin bar and does not count as a major part needing a top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, multi-part lamp. It has 14 visible tones per full tile, which is within the reference range (hedge 9, cheese stall 17, well 20) and well above the crook lamp and bench, which read 0 because they are sparse. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The 25 total colours are higher than the closest reference, the crook lamp (14), though below the stall and well (38-40). The pedestal, post, gold bands and lit lanterns each get roughly 3-4 steps, a little shallower than Beodeul's 5-6. The dark edge pixels are only 52% neutral, so the outline is mixed, not a uniform black sticker line. The lanterns, crown caps and star finial add real structure and a warm/cool contrast. A careful artist would accept it next to the crook lamp without it looking thinner or flatter. It is not as dense as the stall or well, but it is a sparse object and at least as rich as the same-kind lamp reference.
